svg.text: Bandwidth is a trade, not a setting

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The phase detector compares the sampling clock against the data transitions. A bang-bang detector asks only whether the sample was

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: early or late and produces a one-bit answer; a Mueller-Muller detector uses the samples themselves and produces a proportional one.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The first is cheaper and noisier, the second needs decisions and is smoother.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The loop filter sets the bandwidth, and the bandwidth is a genuine trade rather than a tuning knob. Wide tracks the transmitter's

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: wander and passes more jitter through; narrow filters the incoming jitter and cannot follow a drifting clock. Every SerDes

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: datasheet quotes a loop bandwidth for exactly this reason.
